record.paper_title: Some open problems in dynamical systems
record.original_question: Does there exist a connected simply connected manifold M^n that admits a partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism?

evidence.quote: b) Does there exist a connected and simply connected manifold Mn with a partially hyperbolic diﬀeomorphism ?

artifact.status_search_result: The question appears to remain open in general. It is known that the 3-sphere (and more generally compact 3-manifolds with finite fundamental group) admits no partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism, but no example or general nonexistence result has been established for simply connected manifolds in arbitrary dimension. Recent literature on partially hyperbolic systems still treats topological obstructions and the classification of admissible manifolds as active research.

status_evidence.title: Partial hyperbolicity - Scholarpedia
status_evidence.snippet: Topological restrictions imposed by partially hyperbolic splittings; open questions on which manifolds admit such diffeomorphisms.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of manifolds admitting partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms remains an active and largely open problem.

status_evidence.title: Partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms of 3-manifolds with Abelian fundamental groups
status_evidence.snippet: There are no partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms on S^3; more generally, compact 3-manifolds with finite fundamental group admit none.
status_evidence.claim: In dimension 3 the simply connected case is settled negatively (no partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism on S^3), but higher dimensions remain unaddressed.

status_evidence.title: Partially Hyperbolic Diffeomorphisms Homotopic to the Identity in Dimension Three
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work continues to study topological constraints (e.g., virtually solvable fundamental groups) on partially hyperbolic dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Topological obstructions to partial hyperbolicity continue to be the subject of recent research.
